question: A bottling plant's capping robot presses on a 97 kg fixture in a hall 40 m long. The fixture accelerates at a rate in metres per second squared equal to the greatest common divisor of 60 and 286. Find the force in newtons needed to accelerate the fixture, then subtract 27 N supplied by a return spring to get the robot's own contribution. The plant has 7 such robots per line, 9 lines, and 3 identical shifts. Multiply the per-robot contribution by 7, then by 9, then by 3. What is the total force contributed by the robots in N?

A cable-car maintenance team tests a counterweight carriage of mass 18 kg. The carriage's acceleration in metres per second squared is 30 more than the greatest common divisor of 246 and 400. Find the force in newtons that gives the carriage that acceleration. The haul rope carries 12 such carriages at once, so multiply the force by 12, and convert the result to kilonewtons. The system has 3 identical haul ropes, so multiply by 3. What is the total force in kN?

The number the crash-lab technician records is the total energy in kilojoules absorbed by a barrier over 3 identical impacts, after correcting each impact for the sled's release latch. The sled has a mass of 35000 g and a length of 2 m. It strikes the barrier at a speed in metres per second equal to the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 11x + 24 = 0. Find the sled's kinetic energy in joules and subtract 27 J for the energy absorbed by the release latch. Multiply the corrected value by 3 for the 3 impacts and convert the total to kilojoules. What is the recorded total in kJ?

A rail-yard shunting rig pushes a 99 kg test wagon along a 15 m track. The wagon accelerates at a rate in metres per second squared equal to the area under the curve 3x^2 + 6x between x = 0 and x = 1. Find the force in newtons needed to accelerate the wagon. The rig's load cell adds 11 N for rolling resistance and then subtracts 26 N for the assistance of the track's slight downhill grade. The rig has 10 identical wagons on the track, so multiply the per-wagon figure by 10, and then add 10 N for the coupling drag. What is the total force in N?

A quarry haul truck's test trailer has a mass of 136000 g. Its acceleration in metres per second squared is 26 more than the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 10x + 21 = 0. Find the force in newtons needed to accelerate the trailer and convert it to kilonewtons. The truck tows 9 identical trailers, so multiply by 9. An 18 kN assist from the loading ramp's winch is subtracted from that total. What is the net force the truck must supply in kN?

A 97000 g ice-resurfacing sled on a rink 60 m long is pushed with an acceleration in metres per second squared equal to the greatest common divisor of 159 and 156. Find the pushing force in newtons. Subtract 17 N of assistance from the sled's blade lift, and convert the result to kilonewtons. Then add 5 kN for the preload on the sled's tow bar. What is the tow-bar load in kN?

A robot arm on an assembly line moves a 25 kg gearbox casing along a 3 m guide. The casing accelerates at a rate in metres per second squared equal to the rate of change of the curve 5x^3 - 2x^2 with respect to x at x = 1. Find the force in newtons needed to accelerate the casing. The arm must also overcome 23 N of guide friction, so add 23 N, and a balance spring contributes 1 N, so subtract 1 N. Express the arm's required force in kilonewtons. What is it in kN?

The value a shipyard technician records is the corrected energy in kilojoules for a 9 shot test series, after a single 5 kJ deduction for the launch cradle. In each shot a 40 kg lifeboat model is launched at a speed in metres per second equal to 6 times the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 13x + 42 = 0. Find the model's kinetic energy in joules, multiply by 9 for all the shots, and convert the total to kilojoules. Then subtract the 5 kJ deduction. What is the recorded energy in kJ?

A 23000 g test drone flies down a corridor 90 m long at a speed in metres per second equal to the rate of change of the curve 5x^3 + 5x^2 with respect to x at x = 1. Find the drone's kinetic energy in joules at that speed, add 19 J for the energy stored in the spinning rotors, and convert the result to kilojoules. The operator has 11 identical drones, so multiply by 11. From the fleet total subtract 19 kJ for the reserve energy that must stay in the batteries. What is the resulting figure in kJ?

A pneumatic bottle-filling line launches a 5000 g bottle along a chute at a speed in metres per second equal to 9 times the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0. Find the bottle's kinetic energy in joules at that speed. The line controller subtracts 27 J for the energy absorbed by the chute's cushion and a further 12 J for the energy lost to air resistance. The line runs 7 identical chutes, so multiply the corrected per-bottle figure by 7. What is the total energy in J?

A battery test rig on a workshop bench 3 m long drives a 10 kg flywheel cart at a speed in metres per second equal to the number of ways of choosing 4 items from a set of 6. Find the cart's kinetic energy in joules and convert it to kilojoules; this is the energy the rig recovers into the battery when the cart is braked. During the same cycle the rig's heater draws 2 kJ from the battery, so subtract 2 kJ. The rig runs 8 identical cycles, so multiply by 8. What is the net change in the battery's energy over the 8 cycles, in kJ (negative if a loss)?

The number a print-shop engineer needs is the combined force in kilonewtons for 6 identical presses, each with 7 identical feed units, each unit driving 4 identical rollers. Each roller has a mass of 7 kg and accelerates at a rate in metres per second squared equal to the number of ways of choosing 3 items from a set of 8. Find the force in newtons needed for one roller, multiply by 4 for the rollers in a unit, and convert to kilonewtons. Multiply by 7 for the units in one press and by 6 for all the presses. What is the combined force in kN?

What the lift installer finally needs is the corrected cable load in kilonewtons for a bank of 5 identical elevators, after a 22 kN allowance for the counterweight ropes is added. Each elevator car has a mass of 148 kg and a cabin height of 2 m. It accelerates upward at a rate in metres per second squared equal to the rate of change of the curve 2x^3 - 2x^2 with respect to x at x = 2. Find the force in newtons needed to accelerate one car, convert it to kilonewtons, multiply by 5 for the bank, and add the 22 kN allowance. What is the corrected load in kN?

A sledge on a bobsleigh test track 400 m long carries a 49000 g instrument package. The sledge's speed in metres per second equals the rate of change of the curve 3x^3 - 2x^2 with respect to x at x = 2. Find the package's kinetic energy in joules at that speed, and add 6 J for the energy stored in its shock mounts. Convert the result to kilojoules. The data logger then subtracts 7 kJ for the energy absorbed by the track's braking straw. What is the final figure in kJ?

A brewery's keg conveyor, which runs at a height of 1 m above the floor, moves 18 kg kegs at a speed in metres per second equal to the area under the curve 5x^2 + 4x between x = 0 and x = 2. Find the kinetic energy of one keg in joules and convert it to kilojoules. The conveyor's energy meter adds 18 kJ for the energy stored in its drive flywheel. The brewery has 8 identical conveyors, so multiply by 8, and then subtract 4 kJ for the energy recovered by the regenerative drive. What is the final energy figure in kJ?

A test track for delivery robots is 80 m long. Each robot has a mass of 25 kg and moves at a speed in metres per second equal to 3 times the sum of 3 and 2. Find the kinetic energy of one robot in joules. A team runs 8 robots at once, and the facility has 6 identical teams; multiply by 8 and then by 6. Convert the total to kilojoules. What is the total kinetic energy in kJ?

A high-speed rail test facility runs a 43 kg instrumented bogie along a 2 km guideway. The bogie moves at a speed in metres per second equal to 10 times the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 11x + 30 = 0. Find the bogie's kinetic energy in joules at that speed. The facility runs 4 bogies per train, 3 trains per session, and 2 sessions per day; multiply by 4, then by 3, then by 2. What is the total kinetic energy for the day in J?

The number the arena manager needs is the total energy in kilojoules for 11 identical shows, each using 9 identical stage lifts. Each lift carries 4 identical platforms; each platform has a mass of 43 kg, is 2 m wide, and moves at a speed in metres per second equal to the greatest common divisor of 41 and 286. Find one platform's kinetic energy in joules, multiply by 4 for the platforms on a lift, and convert to kilojoules. Multiply by 9 for the lifts in one show, and then by 11 for all the shows. What is the total in kJ?

The figure the freight-yard controller wants is the total energy in kilojoules for 6 identical trains, each of 7 identical wagons. Each wagon in the yard's scale model has a mass of 31 kg and moves at a speed in metres per second found by taking 8 times the sum of 4 and 3 and then adding 14. Find the kinetic energy of one wagon in joules, multiply by 7 for one train, then by 6 for all the trains, and convert the total to kilojoules. What is the total in kJ?

The final number a launch-site engineer records is the energy in kilojoules for 5 identical firings, each corrected for spring storage and pad losses. In each firing a 42 kg test capsule is propelled at a speed in metres per second equal to the second derivative of 2x^3 - 3x^2 with respect to x evaluated at x = 4. Find the capsule's kinetic energy in joules and convert it to kilojoules. Add 28 kJ for the energy stored in the launch spring, then subtract 7 kJ for the energy lost in the pad. Multiply the corrected figure by 5 for all the firings. What is the recorded total in kJ?

A parcel-sorting robot pushes a 7000 g parcel across a sorting deck that is 15 m wide. The parcel's acceleration in metres per second squared is 29 more than the greatest common divisor of 125 and 397. Find the force in newtons needed for one parcel. Each robot pushes 9 parcels at once, so multiply by 9 and convert to kilonewtons. The sorting centre has 12 identical robots, so multiply by 12. What is the total force in kN?

A hospital's pneumatic tube system sends 23 kg specimen carriers along a run that is 140 m long. Each carrier travels at a speed in metres per second equal to the greatest common divisor of 236 and 372. Find the kinetic energy of one carrier in joules. The system launches 9 carriers in a batch, so multiply by 9, and convert the total to kilojoules. The compressor stores a further 30 kJ per batch, so add 30 kJ. The hospital runs 11 identical batches per day, so multiply by 11. What is the day's total energy in kJ?

The final number the range safety officer wants is the corrected energy in joules of a single projectile after four adjustments. The projectile has a mass of 45 kg and a diameter of 15 cm. It leaves the launcher at a speed in metres per second equal to the number of ways of choosing 2 items from a set of 9. Find its kinetic energy in joules. The officer then adds 9 J for the energy stored in the sabot, subtracts 2 J for the energy lost to the muzzle brake, subtracts 18 J for air drag near the muzzle, and adds 16 J for the energy released by the propellant's afterburn. What is the corrected energy in J?

What the pump-test engineer ultimately needs is the total energy in joules for 4 identical test runs, each run comprising 3 identical slugs of fluid. Each slug has a mass of 42000 g and moves at a speed in metres per second equal to the area under the curve 4x^2 + 7x between x = 0 and x = 3. Find the kinetic energy of one slug in joules, subtract 27 J for the energy lost in the inlet valve, and multiply by 3 for the slugs in one run. Add 3 J for the energy stored in the run's accumulator, then multiply by 4 for all the runs. What is the total in J?

The number the toy-factory engineer wants is the total energy in joules for 2 identical test rigs, each of which runs 5 identical carts and carries a 6 J buffer allowance. Each cart has a mass of 6000 g and moves at a speed in metres per second equal to the sum of the whole numbers from 1 to 4. Find the kinetic energy of one cart in joules and add 4 J for the energy stored in its wind-up spring. Multiply by 5 for the carts on one rig, add the rig's 6 J buffer allowance, and multiply by 2 for both rigs. What is the total in J?
